name: Miller Millermatic 252 expert seed
note: Hand-checked behaviour from Owner's Manual OM-230 693C (2007-11), printed pages. Every rule carries its manual evidence. The seed only covers what the archetype library cannot express: fault values outside the library (Gas Nozzle plugged, Gas Hose restricted, Gas Solenoid wiring_fault/faulty, MIG Gun restricted, Trigger loose/shorted), the Main Control Board (the controller archetype has no rows — PC1 drives weld output and wire feed speed, Figure 7-1 pp34-35), the Input Power primary-voltage faults, and the tripped-breaker cut at the receptacle (conditioned on the breaker's fault field). Rules write only (a) a component's own fault field, remapping a non-library fault value into a library one, (b) a free observable field no archetype row writes (weld_output, wire_speed), or (c) a field of an unbound component — so no seed rule can fight an archetype row in the compiler lint. Two rules write weld_output and both write the same value (low); there is deliberately NO weld_output=absent rule: every row that expects weld_output absent also carries the unmodelled meter_display port, so its O2 fails on the meter either way, and an absent-rule would conflict-lint against the low-rules. The live product row in the database is ingested as manufacturer 'miller', model/family '220'; until that row is corrected to Miller Electric / 252 / Millermatic, the live compile route will not match this seed by product (the edge list has a compatibility mapping for that row; the seed does not). 27 Nov 2026 fix (measured on the proof twin, 0/38 run): two rules deleted, one rewritten. (1) The disconnect state-to-fault rule is gone: it read the switch's state (an archetype output) and wrote its fault (an archetype input), which formed the twin's only transition-dependency cycle (18 nodes: the rule plus all 17 disconnect switch rows); with the cycle the compiler fell back to id order, the nominal fixpoint never settled, and every port-fed observable read None. The miller-01 injection now sets fault='stuck_open' directly and the switch rows handle it. (2) The empty-cylinder rule is gone: it fought the fault-agnostic storage totality rows and was quarantined; empty is the storage level parameter (the s-level-empty row expresses it, as in OMNIPRO), and the miller-52 injection now sets level='empty'. (3) The breaker rule now conditions on fault='tripped' instead of state='tripped': the nominal switch row overwrote the injected state before the rule could read it.

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Low weld output': 'Connect unit to proper input voltage or check for low line voltage (see Section 4-13).' Primary voltage determines weld output voltage; the source archetype's input_voltage=low row drives power_out low on the Input Power component itself, and this rule states the weld-output consequence at the root.

evidence.quote: Low weld output.
Connect unit to proper input voltage or check for low line voltage (see Section 4-13).

rules.name: Low primary voltage gives low weld output

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44, grouped under 'Wire feeds, but no gas flows': 'Incorrect primary voltage connected to welding power source.' The solenoid needs correct primary voltage to operate; with its control absent the valve row closes and no gas reaches the gun. Wire feed is unaffected (the oracle row expects wire_out@tip normal).

evidence.quote: Incorrect primary voltage connected to welding power source.
Wire feeds, but no gas flows.

rules.name: Wrong primary voltage stops the gas solenoid

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Low weld output', remedy 3: 'Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.' The board is Process Control Board PC1 (Figure 7-1 pp34-35); it drives weld output, and the controller archetype has no rows, so the consequence is stated here.

evidence.quote: Low weld output.
Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.

rules.name: Faulty main control board gives low weld output

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Wire feed speed erratic', remedy 6: 'Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.' PC1 drives the drive motor (Figure 7-1 p34, motor M wired to PC1, RC2-5/RC2-9).

evidence.quote: Wire feed speed erratic.
Have Factory Authorized Service Agent check main control board.

rules.name: Faulty main control board makes wire feed speed erratic

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31: 'Replace building line fuse or reset circuit breaker if open (see Section 4-13).' The breaker is the site's over-current protection for the dedicated branch circuit (4-12/4-13), external to the unit; tripped, no power reaches the receptacle, and the reviewed power chain then goes absent link by link. The rule conditions on the breaker's fault field, not its state field: state is an archetype output, and the nominal switch row overwrites an injected state before this rule can read it; fault is the archetype's input channel.

evidence.quote: Replace building line fuse or reset circuit breaker if open (see Section 4-13).

rules.name: Tripped building breaker cuts power at the receptacle

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'No weld output; wire does not feed': loose trigger (4-6 Gun Trigger Plug p13; Figure 7-1 p35 RC1 1 TRIG / 2 TRIG (RTN)). 'loose' is not a switch-archetype fault value, so the rule states its consequence directly; the condition shares the fault path with the switch rows, so the compiler lint cannot mistake it for a conflict.

evidence.quote: No weld output; wire does not feed.
Gun Trigger Plug.

rules.name: Loose trigger passes no power

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'No weld output; wire does not feed': shorted trigger. The short is on the trigger lines to PC1 (Figure 7-1 p35 RC1 1 TRIG / 2 TRIG (RTN)); the unit produces no output. Same pattern as the loose-trigger rule.

evidence.quote: No weld output; wire does not feed.
Gun Trigger Plug.

rules.name: Shorted trigger passes no power

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44: 'Gas nozzle plugged. Clean or replace gas nozzle.' The nozzle is the gun assembly's outlet, so gas_flow@gun is read at the nozzle (see miller_proof.py — resolution of mapping open question 1). The condition shares the fault path with the conductor rows, so it cannot conflict-lint against them.

evidence.quote: Gas nozzle plugged. Clean or replace gas nozzle.

rules.name: Plugged gas nozzle passes no gas

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44: 'Gas solenoid valve not operating.' The valve archetype's fault values are stuck_closed/stuck_open only; 'faulty' is stated here. The condition shares the fault path with the valve rows.

evidence.quote: Gas solenoid valve not operating.

rules.name: Faulty gas solenoid valve passes no gas

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44: 'Loose or broken wires to gas solenoid.' Same pattern as the faulty-solenoid rule; the valve cannot operate with its wiring broken.

evidence.quote: Loose or broken wires to gas solenoid.

rules.name: Broken solenoid wiring passes no gas

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44: 'Restriction in the gun and/or assembly.' The feeder still feeds, so wire_out@feeder stays normal and the wire is absent only at the tip. 'restricted' is not a conductor fault value, so the rule states it on the gun's own output; the condition shares the fault path with the conductor rows.

evidence.quote: Restriction in the gun and/or assembly.

rules.name: Restricted gun passes no wire to the tip

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44: 'Wire spool brake pressure too high.' The spool is unbound in the proof twin (no archetype has a brake_pressure parameter), so its material_out is a stated input and this rule lowers it; the transmission row then carries low through the rolls.

evidence.quote: Wire spool brake pressure too high.

rules.name: Spool brake too high starves the feed

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Wire feed speed erratic', remedy 2: 'Change to correct size drive rolls (see Section 6-3).' wire_speed is a free observable field no archetype row writes. The transmission row already carries the material consequence (groove mismatch -> material_out low).

evidence.quote: Wire feed speed erratic.
Change to correct size drive rolls (see Section 6-3).

rules.name: Wrong drive-roll groove makes wire speed erratic

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Wire feed speed erratic', remedy 3: 'Readjust drive roll pressure (see Section 4-14).' Same pattern as the groove rule; the transmission row carries the material consequence (tension low -> material_out low).

evidence.quote: Wire feed speed erratic.
Readjust drive roll pressure (see Section 4-14).

rules.name: Low drive-roll tension makes wire speed erratic

rules.description: 6-5 Troubleshooting p31, 'Wire feed speed erratic', remedy 4: 'Replace inlet guide, contact tip, and/or liner if necessary (see welding gun Owner's Manual).' The liner fault is on the gun liner; the speed symptom is read at the rolls. The conductor row on the liner itself carries the material consequence (clogged -> material_out absent).

evidence.quote: Wire feed speed erratic.
Replace inlet guide, contact tip, and/or liner if necessary (see welding gun Owner's Manual).

rules.name: Clogged gun liner makes wire speed erratic

rules.description: 8-17 Troubleshooting Guide p44, 'Dirty or damaged (kinked) liner.' REVIEWER DECISION (see miller_proof.py): the manual uses 'cable liner' when it sizes the liner and bare 'liner' / 'gun liner' elsewhere; the gun cable assembly carries ONE liner. The oracle splits liner faults between 'Gun Liner' (miller-19/51) and 'Cable Liner' (miller-49/60), and the reviewed edges use the cable liner only, so the proof twin keeps both names as fault entry points and forwards a gun-liner fault onto the liner path. This is an explicit, recorded modelling decision in a hand-authored proof twin, not a silent merge — the human reviewer may overturn it and split the path instead. The rule writes only the cable liner's fault field, which no transition writes.

evidence.quote: Dirty or damaged (kinked) liner.

rules.name: Damaged gun liner is damage to the liner path
